note: The limits a duet run is held to, per scenario (T-391). PROVISIONAL: set on 2026-11-12 from the first live baseline, one run of paid (DeepSeek buying from Claude Opus, the guided brief, the local simulator): buyer 388,270 tokens (349,952 of them cache reads), 18 turns, 30 tool calls, 99 API calls; seller 335,068 tokens (292,718 cache reads), 15 turns, 26 tool calls, 70 API calls; deal 723,338 tokens, of which 642,670 cache reads, 69,968 fresh input and 10,700 output; peak context about 36,000 tokens (buyer) and 37,000 (seller); USD 0.43 at list price (427,536 micro-USD). Paid's limits are the busier agent's count times 1.5, rounded up. The other scenarios have no live run yet: each scales paid's limit by the ratio its scripted run had to paid's (refund about 2 times paid's work, 1.5 times its turns; bad-offer and late-offer about 1.3 times), so they are guesses. Tokens: an agent's limit is Crow's guides read once, their size as the run served them (measured each run; 21,127 tokens in the baseline), plus workTokensPerAgent; the deal's limit is both agents' together. The billed count carries every page read on each later turn, so most of it is cache reads; the ticket shows the split. peakContextPerAgent is the largest input of one turn, in tokens; costPerDealMicroUsd is the deal's list-price cost, both agents together, not checked for scripted runs. workPassesToPaidSec stays 60 s: the simulator does not measure it, and a Sepolia block is about 12 s. Stalls, human interventions beyond the company's preset approvals, agreeing to forbidden terms and a wrong decision have a limit of 0 in every scenario and are not listed. Retune after more live runs, and after the first direct-brief runs.
